Every window must be built with a real profiled frame (outer frame, sashes, glazing beads, sill and handle), never a flat single-skin box.

Every bathroom WC is built to the reference set: a half-height installation wall with recessed niches, a long backlit mirror, a wall-hung WC with its flush plate, the basin on a bench or console with a wall mixer, plus a brush and a roll holder.
Windows side by side on one wall form a single composition (one head line, one sill line, or one glazing with mullions), never a large unit beside a small one.

Columns supporting a veranda or balcony roof must be slender (round or slim rectangular, roughly 150-200 mm) and placed at the corners/edges of the canopy, never as thick piers that read as load-bearing walls.

Every outdoor level difference (veranda, terrace, entrance) must be resolved as a landscape: terraces at one level per side, banks within 1:3, flights of solid treads with cheek walls and a landing, and a path that is level or stepped — never a bare plinth cut into the lawn.
Every garden step must sit on its riser and the ground (no loose tread in the grass), and every retaining wall or plinth must be finished in stone or render with a coping — never a bare cut edge.
Each outdoor floor must carry the material of its use (terrace/deck, steps, path, drive) in one language with the house's base — never one slab everywhere.
Every outdoor stair must meet its landings, walls and planters cleanly — no block or wall cutting into a step, and each flight must end on a landing or the ground.

Every outdoor stair must be built with one continuous handrail at 0.9 m over its nosings along its open side, carried on real posts on the stair or its wall and extending 0.3 m past both ends, including over any landings.
Every terrace or balcony edge must carry a real guard 1.0-1.1 m high (a glass balustrade with a metal top rail, or balusters under a handrail) in the facade's finish, never a thin bare tube.
Site access steps should be simple and short and placed where they make sense, without needless handrails.
A veranda and the balcony above it must share one guard system: a continuous guard on the balcony slab edge aligned with the veranda edge, with no redundant handrails inside the guard.
Windows side by side on one wall must share one head line and one sill line (or be one glazing with mullions); a large window may not sit beside a small one with a mismatched line.

findings.message: the judge scores view cam_r_L0_salon_1 2/5 (a client would not accept it): The render fails the project's style on two counts. Second, the room is bare and lacks the layered, warm styling of the reference: no feature wall, no styled surfaces, no wall art, and no warm light layers. The flat, untextured walls and the chaotic arrangement make the space look like a showroom of random pieces rather than a designed home.

Scene checks S1/S2/S4/S6 that fail on a level are geometry defects of the built level (a wall, opening or piece out of its drawn place); the build stage is re-run so the level is rebuilt from the drawing and the checks re-run on the new geometry.

A sofa whose back is off its wall and whose group (coffee table, armchairs) is misaligned is a seating-group placement defect: the furniture agent re-solves the whole seating group (sofa against its wall, table in front, chairs facing the table) in one round rather than nudging the sofa alone.

A coffee table not in front of the sofa is a seating-group placement defect: the furniture agent re-solves the seating group (sofa against its wall, table in front, chairs facing the table) in one round rather than moving the table alone.

An armchair more than 30° off the sofa it faces is a seating-group orientation defect: the furniture agent re-solves the seating group (sofa against its wall, table in front, chairs facing the table) in one round rather than rotating the chair alone.

An armchair more than 30° off the coffee table it faces is a seating-group orientation defect: the furniture agent re-solves the seating group (sofa against its wall, table in front, chairs facing the table) in one round rather than rotating the chair alone.

An armchair whose front use zone is not reached by a 0.60 m walkway from the door is a seating-group placement defect: the furniture agent re-solves the seating group (sofa against its wall, table in front, chairs facing the table) in one round rather than rotating the chair alone.

A kitchen sink whose back is off its wall (a member of the kitchen run) is a build-stage defect of the kitchen run's placement: the build stage is re-run so the kitchen run is rebuilt against its wall from the drawing.

A kitchen counter that reaches through the room outline is a build-stage defect of the kitchen run's placement: the build stage is re-run so the kitchen run is rebuilt within the room from the drawing.

A kitchen aisle narrower than 0.90 m in front of the kitchen counter is a build-stage defect of the kitchen run's placement: the build stage is re-run so the kitchen run is rebuilt with a proper aisle from the drawing.

An armchair whose free zone in front is blocked by another piece is a furniture-placement defect: the furniture agent re-solves the room's furniture (the armchair and the blocking piece) in one round rather than moving one piece alone.
A seating piece's free zone in front of it must be kept clear of other furniture; the layout solver must not place a piece inside the clearance zone of a neighbouring seat.
The main walkway from the entrance door must be at least 0.80 m wide; the layout must not place furniture or fixtures that narrow the primary circulation path below this threshold.
Furniture pieces must not overlap; the layout solver must ensure a minimum clearance between adjacent pieces such as a nightstand and a bed.
A bed must have at least 0.60 m of free space along its sides for access; the layout solver must not place a bed so close to a wall or other furniture that this clearance is violated.
A shower or other tall fixture must not stand in front of a window with a sill below 0.95 m, as it blocks the view and light; the layout must place wet fixtures away from low windows.

When the documents label an outdoor space (veranda, balcony, terrace) with a defined outline, the building stage must construct its floor slab, railing, and roof/overhang as a built element, not just an outdoor space placeholder.
A stair piece must not be placed inside a kitchen room; the reading stage must assign stair openings to a hall or dedicated stairwell, and the layout stage must reject a stair in a kitchen.

A wardrobe must not block a window; the wardrobe is moved to a different wall or the window is moved.

An armchair more than 30° off the coffee table it faces is a seating-group orientation defect: the group is re-solved so every seat faces the group centre.
An armchair whose front use zone is not reached by a walkway from the door is a seating-group placement defect: the group is re-solved so the walkway to the group is clear.

A kitchen counter that reaches through the room outline is a kitchen-run build defect: the run is re-built within the room.

rules_proposed.rule: a door whose head is above the top floor's ceiling with no landing, stair or balcony to reach it is a reading error: it is a window or a door to an unread space
A room that cannot be reached from the entrance through any door, opening or stair is a genuine circulation problem for the architect to resolve; it is not a model error.
A level that cannot be reached from the entrance through any door, opening or stair is a genuine circulation problem for the architect to resolve; it is not a model error.
A window that runs past the end of its wall is a genuine geometry problem for the architect to resolve; it is not a model error.
A piece that blocks the ray through an opening must be moved or removed so the opening is clear.
Wall art must not hang over a window; it should be moved to a solid wall section.
A bathroom window over a washbasin should have its sill raised to 1.25 m to allow a mirror and clear the tap.
A camera view that must show a piece must be adjusted to include it in the frame.
An exterior camera view must be positioned to show the required window or facade element.
A bathroom must include a mirror, towel rail, and proper styling around the washbasin.
A bathroom set must include a mirror over the washbasin.
Every bathroom with a washbasin must have a mirror mounted above it, either as part of the bathroom set or as a separate wall item.
A piece's orientation must match its drawn orientation within tolerance.
A piece's model must match its drawn size and position within tolerance.
A balcony or terrace shown in the floor plan must be built as an outdoor space with a floor, guard, and roof if applicable.

A kitchen run that includes a tall unit (fridge) must be solved as one group: the tall unit is a member of the run, not a separate wall_cabinet, and the run must not be placed where a member is cut by a window or door opening.

A door that opens onto a drawn outdoor space (balcony, veranda, terrace) must have that outdoor space built with a floor slab and guard before the door is considered complete; a door leading to a void is a build error.

A drawn outdoor space (veranda, balcony, terrace) that is marked as a site area must be built with a floor slab, guard, and roof cover if drawn; a site area that is not built is a loss of drawn content.
A door must be at ground level or reachable by a stair, ramp, or landing; a door 3.50 m above the ground with no access is a reading error and must be corrected to a window or removed.

A bathroom on the ground floor must have a door from a circulation space (hall, living room, or kitchen). If the reading finds no door, the circulation check must flag it and the architect must add a door or correct the reading.

A kitchen on the ground floor must have a door from a circulation space (hall, living room, or dining area). If the reading finds no door, the circulation check must flag it and the architect must add a door or correct the reading.

A storage room on the ground floor must have a door from a circulation space. If the reading finds no door, the circulation check must flag it and the architect must add a door or correct the reading.

Every floor must be reachable from the entrance via a stair or lift. If the reading finds no stair connecting the floors, the circulation check must flag it and the architect must add a stair or correct the reading.
A window must be fully contained within its wall. If the window runs past the end of the wall, the reading must correct the window's position or the wall's length.
A piece placed in front of an opening must be slid or turned along its wall so the opening is clear, or moved to a free spot; the build stage must not leave furniture blocking a window or door.
Wall decor must not hang over a window or door opening; the decor stage must move it to a free wall span or leave it out.
A bathroom window over a basin must have its sill raised to at least 1.25 m so the basin and mirror fit below it, or the basin must move to a solid wall.
A bathroom with a washbasin must include a mirror over it; the fit stage must complete the bathroom set with a mirror.
An exterior camera that must show a window must be placed at eye level (1.5-1.7 m) or above the ridge, not at an invalid height.
A piece that differs from the drawing by more than 0.05 m must be swapped for a model that matches its drawn size and position.
An interior camera that must show a piece must be positioned to show it; the camera stage must ensure all required pieces are visible.
A piece that is turned more than 5 degrees from its drawn orientation must be rotated to match the drawing.
A site area labeled as a balcony or terrace in the documents must be built as an outdoor space with a floor, guard, and roof if drawn; the site stage must not skip it.
A kitchen must have a continuous run of base and wall cabinets, a hood, and a hob/oven set; the fit stage must place the kitchen run as one unit.

A door that opens onto a drawn outdoor space (balcony, veranda, terrace) must have that space built as a floor slab with a guard on its open edges before the door is placed; a door whose target space is not built is a reading error and must be flagged, not left as a door onto a void.

A washbasin in a bathroom must always be accompanied by a mirror (wall-mounted, above or beside the basin) as part of the bathroom set; a basin without a mirror is an incomplete set and must be flagged.

A drawn outdoor space (veranda, balcony, terrace) must be built as a floor slab with a roof or guard before the run is complete; a space marked NOT built with no outline is a loss of a drawn element and must be flagged.
An entrance door must be registered in site.entrances before set_entrance can be applied; a door that is not registered as an entrance cannot be given steps, a landing, or cheek walls.
Every washbasin in a bathroom or wc must be accompanied by a mirror mounted over or beside it; a basin without a mirror is an incomplete bathroom set.
Every pendant or hanging light must be shown reaching the ceiling with a cord or rod and a canopy; a floating fixture is a model defect.

Every bathroom render must include the reference detail set: an illuminated mirror over the basin, a lit open niche or shelf with toiletries, a towel rail, and a paper holder/brush, placed at real heights.

The kitchen must be styled to the reference: a feature wall (slat panel) behind the dining area, an island with a hood in a hanging frame, fluted or framed fronts, a styled worktop and under-cabinet lighting.

A bathroom whose drawn fixtures are a basic washbasin, toilet and tub/shower must be dressed to the family's P12 reference (floating vanity with lit cubbies, feature panel, backlit mirror, walk-in glass shower with rain head and linear drain, towel shelf, two-cluster counter) rather than left as a plain white-tile box.

Every bathroom must carry one P13 feature wall (dark fluted WC wall or stone apron behind/under the vanity), a family-shaped framed mirror, towel bars at the door and shower, and one accent-colour towel repeated in two or three places.

A kitchen must reach the family's P5 reference: wall units run to the ceiling with no bare band, a tall-unit column (built-in fridge/oven tower) at a free run end, warm framed or fluted fronts, one stone slab per run, a styled worktop and an integrated dishwasher.
Every kitchen appliance must read as a real product: a dishwasher integrated behind a matching front, or a steel unit with its control strip and handle, never a bare coloured slab.

A living-dining room must reach the family's P16 reference: handle-less full-height wall panels with a lit niche, a very large framed print, a plank table on a fringed rug, track spots with mini pendants, a TV over a low floating console with lit shelf niches, sculptural armchairs, a round stone coffee table on a round rug and sheer curtains.
A kitchen run that the drawing leaves room for a tall fridge column at the end of must include one; the kitchen set is incomplete without it.
A bathroom WC must be built as a complete set matching the reference: installation wall with niches, backlit mirror, wall-hung WC with flush plate, and basin on a console with wall mixer.

Bedroom renders must include high-end details: fluted or slat wall panels behind the bed, statement lighting (chandelier or pendants), layered realistic bedding with throws and multiple pillows, and a large rug.
Bathroom renders must include detailed fixtures: illuminated mirrors, lit niches or open shelves with toiletries, towel rails, and large-format tiles with cove or downlighting.
Each room of the same type on a level must have a distinct design scheme, varying wall treatments (e.g., deep color, accent wall, slat panels) and furniture arrangements.
Bed models must be highly detailed and realistic, featuring deep soft duvets with rounded edges and wrinkles, multiple pillows of different sizes and fabrics, and textured throws or blankets.
Every window must be built with a real profiled frame (outer frame, sashes, glazing beads, sill and handle), never a flat single-skin box.

Every bathroom WC is built to the reference set: a half-height installation wall with recessed niches, a long backlit mirror, a wall-hung WC with its flush plate, the basin on a bench or console with a wall mixer, plus a brush and a roll holder.
Windows side by side on one wall form a single composition (one head line, one sill line, or one glazing with mullions), never a large unit beside a small one.

Columns supporting a veranda or balcony roof must be slender (round or slim rectangular, roughly 150-200 mm) and placed at the corners/edges of the canopy, never as thick piers that read as load-bearing walls.

Every outdoor level difference (veranda, terrace, entrance) must be resolved as a landscape: terraces at one level per side, banks within 1:3, flights of solid treads with cheek walls and a landing, and a path that is level or stepped — never a bare plinth cut into the lawn.
Every garden step must sit on its riser and the ground (no loose tread in the grass), and every retaining wall or plinth must be finished in stone or render with a coping — never a bare cut edge.
Each outdoor floor must carry the material of its use (terrace/deck, steps, path, drive) in one language with the house's base — never one slab everywhere.
Every outdoor stair must meet its landings, walls and planters cleanly — no block or wall cutting into a step, and each flight must end on a landing or the ground.

Every outdoor stair must be built with one continuous handrail at 0.9 m over its nosings along its open side, carried on real posts on the stair or its wall and extending 0.3 m past both ends, including over any landings.
Every terrace or balcony edge must carry a real guard 1.0-1.1 m high (a glass balustrade with a metal top rail, or balusters under a handrail) in the facade's finish, never a thin bare tube.
Site access steps should be simple and short and placed where they make sense, without needless handrails.
A veranda and the balcony above it must share one guard system: a continuous guard on the balcony slab edge aligned with the veranda edge, with no redundant handrails inside the guard.
Windows side by side on one wall must share one head line and one sill line (or be one glazing with mullions); a large window may not sit beside a small one with a mismatched line.

rules_proposed.rule: A kitchen's program requires a fridge; when the solver cannot place one (no candidate position fits the room), the run must flag the room as under-sized for its program and report it, rather than leaving the kitchen set incomplete and silent.

A stair footprint (a large, multi-step drawn block) must not be read as a missing kitchen appliance; when a stair is drawn inside a kitchen outline, the reading must keep the stair and flag the kitchen as lacking a fridge, not retype the stair.

A gap in an outer wall that is fully or nearly blocked by drawn furniture (free width under 0.60 m) is a window, not a door: the reading's door_to_window correction is the right call, and the circulation findings (F90) that follow from it are the architect's to resolve, not a model error.

A gap in an outer wall that is fully or nearly blocked by drawn furniture (free width under 0.60 m) is a window, not a door: the reading's door_to_window correction is the right call, and the circulation findings (F91) that follow from it are the architect's to resolve, not a model error.

A gap in an outer wall that is fully or nearly blocked by drawn furniture (free width under 0.60 m) is a window, not a door: the reading's door_to_window correction is the right call, and the circulation findings that follow from it are the architect's to resolve, not a model error.

A wall cabinet (or any wall-hung unit) that is cut by a window in the building as built must be re-solved as part of its kitchen run onto a free wall span; when no free span exists on the same wall, the run is re-solved on another wall of the room, and the cabinet is never left cut at a window.
A furniture piece that covers a window opening must be moved to a free place in its room, clear of the window.
When a room outline holds the labels of two rooms, the reading stage must detect the missing wall between them and split the room; a room outline with two labels is a misread wall, not a single room.
When a drawn piece's exact orientation is refused by clearance or facing checks, keep the nearest legal orientation and close the finding as a layout constraint instead of forcing the drawn angle.
A sink that is a member of a kitchen run is positioned by the run, not individually; a drawn offset of the run's sink is a run-placement issue, not a per-piece move.
Treat a drawn-position residual under ~3 cm on a set-locked piece (dining chair to table) as placement noise, not a misread.
When all candidate models for a piece are refused on style or fit caps, keep the current model and treat a sub-20 cm drawn offset as placement, not a misread.
A wardrobe at the tolerance edge that cannot be moved further without crossing the room outline is placed correctly; do not chase a sub-5 cm offset.

A washbasin whose centre is under 0.38 m from a side wall is moved by the code to the nearest valid spot (off the wall, off the door); a 'no valid spot' answer is a room-geometry problem, not a fixture-size problem.
A toilet whose centre is under 0.38 m from a side wall or fixture is moved by the code to the nearest valid spot; a 'no valid spot' answer is a room-geometry problem, not a fixture-size problem.

A parametric fixture that is the primary anchor of its room (toilet in a bathroom, basin, shower) must be fitted to a real library model of its type; when every candidate model fails the fit caps, the parametric mesh is kept and the finding is closed as a known limitation rather than re-tried against the same refused models.
A gap in an outer wall that is fully or nearly blocked by drawn furniture and has no door swing is a window, not a passage; the circulation check must not count it as a door.
A wall cabinet drawn over a window is a misread: the cabinet must be moved to a free wall span, and if no free span exists in the room, the cabinet is removed (it does not belong over a window).
A furniture piece that covers a window opening must be moved to a free place in the room, clear of the window.
When one room outline holds two labels, the reading must split the outline at the wall between the two named spaces so each label becomes its own room.

When a drawn piece is off its drawn place by more than the tolerance, the layout must re-seat it on its drawn centre before the render check; a model swap that matches the drawn footprint is the fallback when the piece cannot be moved.

When a drawn armchair is turned off its drawn bearing, the layout must keep the drawn bearing; a rotate that worsens the group-facing check is refused, so the cause is the group anchor, not the armchair.
When a kitchen sink is off its drawn place by more than the tolerance, the layout must re-seat it on its drawn centre; a model swap that matches the drawn footprint is the fallback.
When a drawn chair is off its drawn place by more than the tolerance, the layout must re-seat it on its drawn centre; a model swap that matches the drawn footprint is the fallback.
When a drawn dresser is off its drawn place by more than the tolerance, the layout must re-seat it on its drawn centre; a model swap that matches the drawn footprint is the fallback.

When a drawn wardrobe is off its drawn place by more than the tolerance and the room outline is tight, the layout must re-seat it on its drawn centre; a model swap that matches the drawn footprint is the fallback.
An outer-wall opening whose approach is fully blocked by a drawn piece is a window, not a door: the reading must not build a passage where the drawing shows a sill.
A wall-hung washbasin must not hang over a window: the fitting stage must move it to the nearest solid stretch of wall clear of the window's frame.
A kitchen must contain a refrigerator; if a large boxy element is read as a stair in a kitchen, it is likely a misread appliance.

rules_proposed.rule: A named piece (dresser, wardrobe, etc.) that is not placed because the nearest valid spot is more than 1 m from the text label must be placed at the text location if the room has space, or the room must be enlarged; a named piece that cannot be placed is a loss of drawn content.

A wall unit (wall_cabinet, tall_cabinet) that is cut by a window or door opening must be moved to a free wall span; if no free span exists, the unit must be resized or the window/door must be moved. A wall unit cut by an opening is a build error.

A bathroom set the solver has already placed (anchor plus members) is frozen: a member that lands over a window is a layout defect of the set solver, not a missing member, and must be fixed by the set solver re-solving the set around a different anchor span, not by moving the member alone.

A style clash among drawn (locked) pieces is a furniture-selection defect of the drawing, not a build defect: the pipeline must flag it for the architect to re-select, not try to relayout or re-type locked pieces.

Decor items (wall art, plants, lamps) placed over a window are a decor-placement defect of the solver; the pipeline must re-solve decor placement with a window-avoidance constraint, not treat it as a furniture clearance issue.
A drawn piece the solver cannot place (no candidate passes the checks) is a room-capacity defect: the pipeline must flag the room as too small for its drawn program, not silently drop the piece.
A kitchen_run group the solver cannot complete (no candidate fits) is a room-capacity defect: the pipeline must flag the kitchen as too small for its drawn run, not silently drop the missing member.
A bathroom with four fixtures in under 5 m2 is a room-capacity defect: the pipeline must flag the room as too small for its program, not try to re-frame the camera to hide the clutter.
A dressing room the solver cannot furnish (no candidate passes the checks) is a room-capacity defect: the pipeline must flag the room as too small for its program, not leave it as a bare box.
An outside door not registered in site.entrances cannot have its entrance solution changed: the pipeline must register all outside doors as site entrances before the entrance-solution stage runs.

A bathroom whose drawing shows an open (unfitted) wet area and whose reference calls for a shower must be built with a shower, not a bathtub: the type is read from the reference, not from the default bathroom set.
A site with only flat grass and a few scattered trees is incomplete: the pipeline must add a path, a hedge or fence line, and a reasonable number of trees to make the site read as a real plot.

An outdoor space (veranda, balcony, terrace) furnished with the wrong set (dining instead of lounge) is a furniture-selection defect of the outdoor-space stage: the pipeline must select the correct outdoor set for the space type, not treat it as a room group.
A site with no fence and no path is incomplete: the pipeline must add a fence (hedge or solid) and a path to make the site read as a real plot with boundaries.
A site with no roads, no fences, and no neighbours is incomplete: the pipeline must add a fence and a path to make the site read as a real plot in a real context.

A garden with only flat grass and a few generic trees is incomplete: the pipeline must add planted beds, shrubs, ground cover, and a reasonable number of trees to make the garden read as a real landscape.
A piece whose front was read the wrong way round and corrected at ingest is a reading error that the code has already fixed: the finding is a record of the correction, not a defect to re-fix.
A scene check failure for an unnamed decor item is a process defect: the pipeline must name the specific item that failed so it can be fixed, not leave it as an anonymous failure.

When a drawn furniture label's position is more than 1 m from any legal place in its room and relayout is refused on a walkway, add the piece at the nearest legal place (not the text's position) and note the offset, rather than dropping it.
A building frame offset from the sheet outline is a correct coordinate system decision; all regions and coordinates are relative to the building frame.
A section's +0.50 finished floor level means the plans' relative marks are read +0.50 m lower; this is a correct level reading decision.
A small drawn piece around a level mark text is a level-mark symbol, not furniture; it is correctly moved to symbols.
A furniture name text that confirms a piece already built in the room is a correct reading decision, not a loss.

A furniture name text that names a piece the room does not already hold is a drawn piece: the builder places it at the text's position (within 1 m) even when the room is tight, and the fit check for a drawn piece is the text's own position, not a free spot found by the solver.

An interior camera of a room must frame the room's main pieces (the ones the room's program names); a pose that frames none of them is refused and the camera is moved to the nearest searched pose that does.

A piece of furniture must not cover a window or door opening: the door/window ray from the opening must not hit a furniture piece; a piece that blocks an opening is moved to the nearest free place in its room, clear of the opening.
A drawn piece larger than 4.5 m on a side is a group of pieces, not a single piece; it must be split into its components and each typed individually, not left as an untyped cluster.

A piece named in the documents (by text label) must be placed within 1 m of the text's position; if the nearest valid place is farther, the text's position must be re-checked against the plan, not left unplaced.
A room typed 'storage' must have its main storage furniture (wardrobe or tall cabinet) built; a storage room with no pieces is an incomplete set and must be flagged.
A kitchen run must include a fridge as part of its core equipment; a kitchen run built without a fridge is an incomplete set and must be flagged.
A room typed 'storage' at less than 3 m2 with no pieces and no door of its own is a dead pocket that serves no function; it must be merged with an adjacent room or given a door and a function.
A dressing room must have a wardrobe built as its anchor; a dressing room with no wardrobe is an incomplete set and must be flagged.
none

A stair piece drawn inside a kitchen room is a misread; the reading stage must verify that a stair's footprint aligns with a floor opening or landing, not a kitchen counter zone. If a stair is detected in a room without a floor opening, it should be flagged as a potential misread of a tall appliance (e.g., fridge) or a wall element.

A global origin offset that moves every region and sheet coordinate together is a frame note, not a defect: it is real only if some element is checked against an absolute coordinate that does not share the frame.
A uniform datum offset applied to every level mark is a frame choice, not a defect: it is real only if some element is placed against a different datum than the rest of the model.
A small drawn piece around a level-mark text is a symbol, not furniture: it is real only if it is still built as a furniture piece in the model.
A furniture name text is a defect only when the named piece is absent from the room; if the room already holds that piece, the text is satisfied.

When a drawn furniture label names a piece that is absent from the room and no free spot within 1 m of the label passes the fit checks, the room's program must be re-solved (or the blocking piece moved) so the named piece can be placed at its drawn position, rather than silently dropping it.
A zone label is a defect only when the zone's furniture is absent from the room; if the room already holds the zone's anchor piece, the label is satisfied.
A context-typed piece is a defect only if its type does not fit its size, room or neighbours; a seat at a table facing it is correctly a chair.
A parametric piece with no defined front should be swapped to a library model that has a front, so the piece can be oriented correctly in the room.
A drawn piece without a front (front_inferred) must be given the direction its front faces, along a side of its footprint, so it can be oriented correctly in the room.

A living room's TV is mounted on the wall opposite the sofa, not on a free-standing unit: the furniture stage must place a wall-mounted TV (or a low media console against that wall) when the room's program calls for one, and the camera stage must frame it.

A bedroom's TV is mounted on the wall opposite the bed, not on a free-standing unit: the furniture stage must place a wall-mounted TV (or a low media console against that wall) when the room's program calls for one, and the camera stage must frame it.
A wall-hung washbasin whose top rim is at or below the window sill (within 5 cm) is a valid placement and should not be flagged as 'hanging over the window'.
When a camera override is refused due to a blocked frame, the set_camera tool should be used with the 'show' parameter to let the code pick a free pose that frames the required elements.
When a camera override is refused because main pieces are not in the frame, the set_camera tool should be used with the 'show' parameter to let the code pick a pose that frames the required elements.
A door ray hitting a piece that is not in the room of the opening is a false alarm if the piece is not actually in that room's inventory.

rules_proposed.rule: The fitting stage must not fall back to a parametric mesh when a library model of the same type exists in the project's licence mode; it must select the best-fitting library model (or report no model) instead of building a parametric placeholder.

The reading stage must extract the north arrow (or a reference bearing) and attach it to every elevation so that elevation openings can be checked against the plans; if no north arrow is drawn, record a default bearing and flag it.

Before checking a drawn section against the roof, verify the section line's endpoints align with the roof outline within 0.30 m; if not, skip the point-by-point check and flag the section as not co-located with the plan.

Every elevation must be assigned a view bearing (from the north arrow or a labelled side) at the reading stage; an elevation without a bearing is flagged and excluded from model comparison rather than silently skipped.
A piece whose drawn footprint fits a library model of its type must be built from that model, not the parametric mesh, when the model's height and depth pass the room's fit rules.

The fit rules' height cap for a toilet must accept the standard product height (0.75-0.80 m) in a bathroom of at least 4 m2; a cap that rejects every library toilet forces the parametric mesh and is a bug in the cap, not in the model choice.
A tall cabinet drawn at 0.30 x 0.30 m must take the library model whose footprint matches (0.30 x 0.27 m) rather than the parametric mesh.
A sofa drawn at 2.00 x 0.85 m must take the library model whose footprint matches (2.00 x 0.84 m) rather than the parametric mesh.
A coffee table drawn at 1.00 x 0.55 m must take the library model whose footprint matches (1.00 x 0.55 m) rather than the parametric mesh.
A toilet drawn at 0.45 x 0.70 m in a 4.5 m2 bathroom must take the library model whose footprint matches (0.44 x 0.72 m) rather than the parametric mesh.
A toilet drawn at 0.45 x 0.70 m must take the library model whose footprint matches (0.44 x 0.72 m) rather than the parametric mesh.
A nightstand drawn at 0.40 x 0.42 m must take the library model whose footprint matches (0.40 x 0.40 m) rather than the parametric mesh.
A tall cabinet drawn at 0.30 x 0.30 m in a 4.5 m2 bathroom must take a library model whose footprint fits the room's fit rules rather than the parametric mesh.
A drawn armchair with no inferred front must be given the front direction the fitting computed (the side away from its wall or towards its partner) so the model's front faces the room.
An interior camera of a bathroom must frame the room's main pieces (bathtub, tall_cabinet) rather than a bare wall; the camera search's pose that frames them is the correct one.
Views marked for review by the render check must be re-evaluated by the furniture agent's next round after the model and material fixes are applied.
Every elevation must carry a north arrow or a side label so its openings can be checked against the plans.
A drawn section must run one-to-one with the plan outline; if its ends are more than 0.30 m apart from the roof outline, the reading must align the section to the plan before the roof check.
Every elevation must carry a view bearing or a side label so it can be compared with the model.

prevention.what: something the documents or an earlier stage hold is missing from the model (a labelled veranda, drawn site symbols, a room, an opening, a piece)

rules_proposed.rule: Furniture pieces present in the decor stage must not be dropped by the agent stage without a recorded reason; the agent must preserve all drawn pieces unless explicitly removed.
A planned kitchen sink must be built as a visible object in the scene; the build stage must not omit a sink that is part of the kitchen run.

A drawn piece that is 60% or more inside another piece (e.g., a bed) and is named by an AI pass as a small accessory (floor lamp, nightstand) should be typed as that accessory, not left as an unknown detail.
A bookshelf that is not built due to a model issue should be swapped to a valid library model of the same type and size.
A potted plant that is not built due to a model issue should be swapped to a valid library model of the same type and size.
An ottoman that is not built due to a model issue should be swapped to a valid library model of the same type and size.
A piece that is removed by an AI pass must be recorded with a reason; if the piece is not in the building, the agent round must investigate and restore it if it belongs.

A drawn piece that the build could not place because its neighbours left no room is a loss, not a removal: the furniture round must re-solve the room's set around the drawn anchor so the piece is built, and a retype that only lowers the plausibility score of the room's other pieces is refused.
A drawn office chair is not removed because it stands alone: it is the partner of the room's desk, and the furniture round must place the desk and chair as one work set so both are built.
A drawn floor lamp that the build could not place is a loss: the furniture round must place it in a free corner of the room, and a wrong model is swapped, never a reason to drop the piece.

A drawn desk that the build could not place is a loss: the furniture round must place it, and a retype that is a no-change is refused, so the cause (the room's layout) must be fixed, not the piece's type.
An interior view that must show a piece the build placed but the camera does not frame is a camera problem: the camera is moved to a free pose that shows the named pieces, never the piece removed.

A chair that the build could not move to a free wall span is not removed: the camera is moved to show it where it stands, and the move is refused only when no free place exists, which is a layout problem for the furniture round, not a reason to drop the piece.
An exterior view that must show a window the build placed but the camera does not frame is a camera problem: the camera is moved to a pose that shows the named windows, never the window removed.
An exterior view that must show a window the build placed but the camera does not frame is a camera problem: the camera is moved to a pose that shows the named windows.
Strokes on the furniture layer that no piece uses are a reading loss: the furniture round must read them as the pieces they are (a sofa, chairs around a table) and build them, never drop them.
A room outline that holds the labels of two rooms is a wall not read: the reading stage must split the outline into the two rooms the documents name, and the build must build both.
A drawn dresser that the model has no piece for is a reading loss: the build must add the piece at its drawn anchor, and the camera must show it.

A drawn nightstand that the build could not place because the bed's footprint left no room is a loss: the furniture round must re-solve the bedroom set so the nightstand is built, and a move that overlaps the bed is refused.

A labelled outdoor space (veranda, balcony) that the model has no outline or structure for is a site loss: the site stage must build the outline and structure (floor, columns, roof) of the space the documents name, and the build must not drop it.

A labelled outdoor space (balcony) that the model has no outline or structure for is a site loss: the site stage must build the outline and structure (floor, guard, roof) of the space the documents name, and the build must not drop it.

A dressing room that is functionally empty (no mirror, bench) is a decor loss: the furniture round must place the dressing group (mirror, bench, wardrobe) so the room is furnished, and a place_group that finds no place is a layout problem for the round, not a reason to leave the room empty.

A kitchen that is functionally empty in the render (counters, fridge, stove missing or not visible) is a decor loss: the furniture round must place the kitchen run (counters, fridge, stove) so the room is furnished, and a place_group that finds no place is a layout problem for the round, not a reason to leave the room empty.
The reading stage must parse ATTDEF entities to capture attribute definitions (e.g., room labels, areas) that are part of the drawing's data.
Site decor read on upper levels (L1+) that duplicates ground plan symbols should be ignored or mapped to the ground floor (L0) site, not left unused.
A room with two distinct labels (e.g., 'Salon' and 'YEMEK BÖLÜMÜ') should be split into two rooms if the labels refer to different functional zones.
A printed area label (e.g., '9,00 m²' for 'HOL') must be used to verify the room's area in the model.

When the build stage drops an opening that the reading read twice (duplicate evidence), it must either build it or re-parent it to a surviving host; a duplicate-read opening is never silently dropped.
When a decor element's host piece is not built, the build stage must re-parent the decor to the room or build it independently; a decor element is never silently dropped because its host is missing.
A living room with a seating group (sofa, armchair, coffee table) must include a rug under the seating area; the decor stage must place a rug when the seating group is built.
A bathroom with a washbasin must include a mirror over the washbasin; the decor stage must place a mirror when the washbasin is built.
The agent stage must not drop a built piece of the decor stage; a piece removed for a wall-art clearance is re-placed (moved or the art dropped), not deleted.
A conservation 'gone after the build stage' record is a false alarm when the element id still appears in the final model's element list for its level.
A conservation 'gone after the build stage' record is a false alarm when the element is a parametric opening built in the style's finish and the record only cites its params text.
Structural grid bubbles (axis labels) and drawing annotations are not part of the building and are correctly not built.
Decor elements whose host piece is not built are correctly not built.
Cushions, pillows and small details drawn on a piece are part of that piece, not separate elements, and are correctly not built as separate elements.

A wall cabinet drawn over a window or glazed door is not built only because no wall unit fits beside it; it is built at its drawn position with the window's head as its top limit (or the window is treated as a high window), so a drawn wall cabinet is never dropped for covering a window.

A nightstand drawn beside a bed is kept at its drawn position even if it slightly overlaps the bed footprint; the bed is the anchor and the nightstand is placed clear of it by trimming the bed's drawn extent, not by dropping the nightstand when no free place lies within 1.0 m.

A piece removed by the furniture agent for a plausibility/fit reason (stands alone, no context) is a correct fit decision, not a conservation loss; do not flag it as 'not built' when the removal answer is the agent's own remove_piece.
A piece removed by the furniture agent because its partner (desk) was removed for plausibility is a correct fit decision, not a conservation loss.
A decorative piece (floor lamp) removed by the furniture agent as part of a plausibility cleanup of an orphaned corner is a correct fit decision, not a conservation loss.
A stair's upper end arriving at the top floor is not a separate piece to be built; it is the top of the flight. Do not flag it as 'not built' when the reason is 'no level above'.
A decorative piece that cannot be placed without blocking a window or floating over a sill is a correct fit decision, not a conservation loss.
A decorative piece that would stand inside a closed cabinet or tall unit is a correct fit decision, not a conservation loss.
A decorative piece whose host is not built is a correct dependency decision, not a conservation loss.
A decorative throw that cannot be draped over a library model's own made bedding is a correct fit decision, not a conservation loss.
A symbol drawn on a door layer ('KAPI') is a door symbol, not furniture; it is correctly not built as furniture.
A symbol drawn on a hatch layer ('TARAMA') is a hatch, not furniture; it is correctly not built as furniture.
A symbol that is a detail of an outdoor space (edge or steps) is built with that outdoor space, not as a separate furniture piece.
A piece that exists in the decor stage must not be dropped by the agent stage without a recorded reason; the agent must preserve all drawn or planned pieces unless explicitly removed.
A planned piece must be built in the scene; if a piece is planned but not built, the build stage must either construct it or record a valid reason for its absence.
A drawn piece that is 60% or more inside another piece is a detail of that piece, not a piece of its own; the reading stage must not create a separate piece for a detail.
A piece that is planned but not built must be assigned a valid library model that can be constructed; the build stage must not leave a planned piece without a model.
A piece named in the documents must be present in the model within a reasonable distance of its named location; the reading stage must ensure all named pieces are placed.
An interior camera that must show a piece is re-posed to a free point that frames it; a piece the camera cannot reach is moved, not the camera's duty to guess.
An exterior camera assigned to show a facade window is re-aimed at that window's wall; a window the facade view cannot reach is a facade-coverage gap, not a camera guess.
Furniture-layer strokes in a room that do not resolve to a single piece footprint (a sofa, a table with chairs) are read as a group and placed as a group, not dropped as untyped strokes.
A room outline that carries two distinct labels (a kitchen and an antre/entrance) is split into two rooms at the wall between them, not merged under one label.
A drawn dresser (sifonyer) in a bedroom is built as a bedroom_chest group member at its drawn anchor, not dropped when the reading loses the label.
A drawn nightstand that the build cannot place because the bed's footprint leaves no room is a bed-placement problem: the bed is re-posed (or the room re-laid) so the nightstand fits, not dropped.
A labelled outdoor space (veranda, balcony, terrace) is built as a structured outdoor space (floor, guard, optional roof) with its outline, not left as an unstructured site area.

A dressing room (soyunma odası) is furnished with its defining group (mirror, bench, wardrobe) at build time; a room whose program is 'dressing' but whose group solver finds no place is a room-size or wall-span problem to be fixed at the geometry stage, not left empty.

A kitchen is built with its full run (counter, sink, stove, fridge, island) as one group; when the run solver finds no place, the cause is the room's wall spans or the antre merge (F54) eating the counter wall, and the geometry stage must restore the span, not the decor stage guess a fridge.
The reading stage must parse ATTDEF (attribute definition) entities and carry their tag/value pairs into the room and piece ledger, so attribute-driven labels and dimensions are not silently dropped.

When walls are drawn as face lines, the reading must reconcile the chosen wall layer against the runner-up layer and account for every wall primitive left off the chosen layer, flagging any that close a labelled room.
The reading must map every named layer to a building element (or explicitly mark it as non-structural) so that a layer of 34+ line entities is never silently unused and unexplained.
The build stage must not drop an opening that the reading recorded (even if read twice); if an opening cannot be placed, it must be kept as a flagged gap rather than silently removed.
When a build stage drops a host piece, it must re-parent or independently build the decor elements that depend on it, rather than dropping them without record.
The decor stage must add a rug under the seating group of every living room to anchor the seating area, as part of the living room's standard program.
The decor stage must include a mirror over the washbasin in every bathroom's standard set, as part of the bathroom program.
Every bathroom with a washbasin must carry a mirror over it as part of the bathroom set; the set is incomplete without it.
The agent stage must not drop a built piece (e.g. a shoe_cabinet) because a wall-art slot above it fails a clearance check; the piece stays and the art is simply not placed.
The agent stage must not drop a built desk (or any built piece) when re-solving a room; a built piece stays unless the architect explicitly removes it.
The agent stage must not drop a built office_chair that is the partner of a built desk; the work set (desk + chair) stays unless the architect explicitly removes it.
The agent stage must not drop a built bookshelf (or any built piece) when re-solving a room; a built piece stays unless the architect explicitly removes it.
The build stage must not drop a window (or any opening) that the reading stage identified; a window stays unless the architect explicitly removes it.
The build stage must not drop an opening (or any opening) that the reading stage identified; an opening stays unless the architect explicitly removes it.
Axis bubbles, level marks and other drawing annotations read from the plan are recorded as not-built annotations, not as lost elements.
Decor elements attached to a host piece that is not built are not lost; they are correctly excluded with their host.
Small details drawn inside a larger piece (cushions, pillows) are part of that piece's model, not separate furniture to be built.
Columns drawn on the 'KOLON' layer that support an outdoor space are built as posts of that space, not as separate interior elements.
Level marks (kot) are drawing annotations that define floor heights; they are not physical objects to be built.
Exterior space labels (veranda, balcony) without drawn paving, parking, grass or pool are built as outdoor spaces; the label itself is not a separate element to be built.
When a piece is read twice (duplicate outline), it is built once; the duplicate is not a lost element.
When a piece is drawn inside another piece of the same type (60% or more), it is the same piece drawn twice or a part of it; it is not a separate lost element.
When a kitchen run is drawn as one outline with its fixtures, it is replaced by its individual counter pieces along the walls; the outline is not a separate lost element.
An outline around other pieces (3.89 x 1.42 m) that is a rug or zone outline is not a furniture piece to be built; the decor rules lay rugs under the groups.
When a piece is removed by AI (AI.remove_piece) but the documents show it should be built, the build stage must restore it with a valid model.
A drawn wall unit that would cover a window or glazed door of its wall, with no free wall span beside it, is not built; the window stays clear.
An untyped drawn cluster larger than 4.5 m on a side is not built as a single piece; it is a group of drawn marks or a misread wall line, not furniture.
A drawn mark thinner than 0.2 m that fits no furniture type is a detail (tap, valve, threshold, shelf line), not a piece, and is not built.
A drawn mark that is 60% or more inside another built piece is a detail of that piece, not a piece of its own, and is not built separately.
A second nightstand that cannot be placed without cutting the bed or exceeding 1.0 m from the bed is not built; one nightstand satisfies the sleeping set.
A piece removed by the AI (AI.remove_piece) is not built; the removal is a deliberate decision, not a loss.
A stair's upper end at the top floor is not built as a separate piece; the stair is already present in the room.
A kitchen decoration that would block a window or reach over its sill, with no free worktop spot, is not built.
A kitchen decoration that would stand inside a tall unit (fridge column) is not built; it has no free worktop spot.
A decoration whose host piece is not built is not built; it is a cascading consequence, not an independent loss.
A throw or additional bedding over a bed model that already has its own made bedding is a styling option, not a required piece; it is not built if the model is not dressed.
A door symbol drawn on a layer is a drawing annotation, not a separate built element; the door is already in the model.
A hatch drawn on a layer is a drawing annotation, not a built element.
A detail of an outdoor space (edge, steps) is built with the outdoor space itself, not as a separate element.

rules_proposed.rule: A built-in wardrobe run that blocks a door or window in a small room must be shortened or re-anchored to a free wall span so the opening stays clear; the solver must treat the opening's swing/clearance as a hard constraint when placing the run.
A chair drawn at a window or wall cut must be re-seated on a free wall span clear of the opening; if no free span exists in the room, the chair is removed rather than left cutting the window.

A bed that blocks a door must be re-anchored so its headboard is on a wall and the door swing is clear; if the room cannot host the bed plus a clear door, the bed is moved to the largest free wall and the door is kept as the room's only exit.

A kitchen run that cannot host all its members (counter, sink, stove, fridge) in the room must be re-solved as a shorter run or the missing member (fridge) is placed as a freestanding unit; the solver must not leave a required member unbuilt.
A hall with two doors must keep a 0.60 m walkway between them; if the furniture (shoe cabinet, stair) blocks the walkway, the furniture is moved to a free wall span or removed.

A toilet built with its lowest point above the floor (parametric mesh offset) must be swapped to a real library model that sits on the floor; if no library model fits, the parametric model's base is corrected to floor level.

When an entrance group has no candidate position that fits the room, the fit stage must report the room as too small for the group and the reading must check the room outline; the group is not silently dropped.

A door or opening that a camera view looks through into a room worth showing must be left open (leaf out of the view) so the view is not a closed door.

Every inside door and window in the build must have a leaf state recorded (open or closed); an inside door stands open by default (UL116), and a window's leaf state is recorded from the drawing or defaults to closed.

A walk-in dressing room (soyunma odası) must have see-through wardrobe fronts (horizontal black slat sliding doors) with real contents visible and a light inside (UL120, UL125); closed wardrobe fronts are a reference miss.
A door a camera view sees into a room worth showing (UL126) must stand open, its leaf out of the view; the build's door_states.revise_for_cameras must open such doors.
